subject.title: [Bug] Dashboard Stop button can corrupt session files + agent permission isolation lacks guardrails

question: Should OpenClaw add default per-agent/destructive host-exec guardrails, or keep host exec as a trusted single-operator default and require sandbox, approvals, or separate OS users for stronger isolation?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally allow full trusted host exec by default when sandboxing is unavailable, while the issue reports real cross-agent data loss; changing that boundary affects security posture, compatibility, and operator workflows.

options.title: Split session fix and exec design
options.body: Keep this issue open, land or replace the user-stop/session durability work with proof, and run a separate maintainer security design for host-exec defaults and per-agent state isolation.

options.title: Session-only fix
options.body: Fix Dashboard Stop/session corruption now and leave host-exec isolation as documented operator policy plus audit warnings.

options.title: Harden exec defaults
options.body: Change default host-exec posture to require per-agent/destructive-action approval or sandbox isolation, with migration, doctor messaging, and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Split session fix and exec design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, land or replace the user-stop/session durability work with proof, and run a separate maintainer security design for host-exec defaults and per-agent state isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent overlap across session lifecycle, Gateway abort handling, and security docs, while exec-specific owners should review the policy details.
